answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks through hardware remote attestation. Agents must execute inside secure enclaves, signing actions with factory-fused keys to enter the agent garden. This forces an attacker to incur the verifiable capital cost of provisioning distinct walnut-sized silicon chips per identity. Periodic lantern broadcasts verify enclave measurements on-chain. However, this architecture trusts centralized chip vendors and remains vulnerable to side-channel key leakage.
